outcomes.text: Explain how conventions, forms and techniques create meaning in drama and live theatre.
Explain how creative and artistic choices shape the meaning an audience receives.
Analyse interpretative processes: practical demands of texts, performance space, stage movement and positioning, spatial relationships.
Analyse performer choices: character motivation, vocal and physical interpretation, delivery, listening and response, sub-text, pace, pitch and climax.
Analyse the performer-audience relationship and configuration.
Analyse design of sets, costume, make-up, lighting, sound and props, and fundamentals such as scale, shape, colour and texture.
Explain how genre, form, structure, language, stage directions, character construction and style make a text performable.
Explain how social, cultural and historical contexts inform a text and its interpretation and performance.
Study and explore practically two set plays, one from List A and one from List B.
Adopt the perspective of performer, designer or director (at least two roles for List A; all three for List B).
Explain how a play is constructed to communicate meaning and how its context informs it.

topics.title: 3.1.3 Area of study 2: Live theatre production

outcomes.text: Analyse a production's aims, how well the team met them, and the creative collaboration of performers, designers and director.
Evaluate the audience experience and response.
Explain how performers, designers or the director communicated meaning and how aspects of the piece added to its impact.
Research a production beforehand, and see live theatre that meets the length, cast and production-value requirements.
Choose one specialism: performer, lighting, sound, set, costume or puppet designer, or director.
Create and develop original devised ideas to communicate meaning.
Develop own ideas, research theatre-making methods, apply learning from live theatre and collaborate.
Explore devising and rehearsal methods and refine work in progress.
Study one prescribed practitioner's context, purpose, intentions, innovation, methods, style and influence.
Keep an individual working notebook of the devising process.
Contribute to a devised piece for a live audience as performer, designer or director.
Create and communicate meaning and realise artistic intention in devised drama.
Interpret characters and roles in line with the group's dramatic aims.
Develop vocal skills: accent, diction, pace, pitch, pause, projection, intonation and verse-speaking.
Develop physical skills: movement, posture, gesture, gait, agility, synchronisation and fluidity.
Develop facial expression, eye contact, listening and response.
Develop ensemble and choral skills and spatial awareness; understand performer-audience configuration.
Develop interpretive invention and adopt safe working practices.
Design and realise lighting plots that serve the dramatic aims.
Establish location, time, mood and atmosphere with lighting.
Select equipment such as lanterns, floorlights, strobes and software.
Use colour gels, filters, gauzes, silhouettes and projections effectively.
Create lighting states by manipulating focus, intensity, colour and shadow, working safely.
Create and realise sound designs that serve the dramatic aims.
Establish location, time, mood and atmosphere through sound.
Select equipment such as microphones, amplifiers, software and instruments.
Make and choose recordings of sound and music.
Manipulate levels, reverb, echo, effects, fades, soundscapes and music, working safely.
Design and realise sets that serve the dramatic aims and create opportunities for performers.
Choose staging forms and use space, scale, levels and perspective effectively.
Plan for action and traffic: entrances, exits, projections and scene changes.
Choose furnishings, textures, materials and colours, and construction for durability and safety.
Design and realise costumes that serve the dramatic aims and establish character.
Establish period, location, mood and atmosphere through costume.
Choose materials, fabric, texture, trimmings and accessories.
Show understanding of colour, shape, fit, period detail, authenticity, movement and ornamentation.
Design make-up and hair suited to character, period, age and ethnicity, choosing suitable materials.
Design and realise puppets that serve the dramatic aims.
Choose a puppet style: marionette, shadow, hand or human-arm.
Create a puppet with defined character, size, scale, shape and texture.
Choose costume, body, head and limbs; make a durable puppet easy to manipulate, working safely.
Develop directorial strategies that serve the dramatic aims and communicate meaning.
Develop inventiveness and clarity of vision.
Explore material through rehearsal and devising methods.
Choose and configure performance spaces and performer-audience relationships.
Apply rehearsal techniques to movement, spatial relationships, use of space and set.
Create pace, tempo, rhythm and climax, working safely.

units.title: 3.4 Guidance on theatrical skills and practitioners

outcomes.text: Select one prescribed practitioner for devising (Component 2) and a different one for making theatre (Component 3).
Know directors and ensemble makers such as Brook, Donnellan, Doran, Elliott, Findlay, Goold, Hytner, Lloyd, Norris, Rice and Rourke.
Know Artaud, Boal, Brecht, Craig, Grotowski, McGrath, Meyerhold, Stanislavski and Pilbrow.
Know physical and multimedia companies such as Berkoff, Complicite, DV8, Frantic Assembly, Gecko, Kneehigh, 1927 and Forkbeard Fantasy.
Know Alecky Blythe, Fo and Rame, Godber, Nicholas Kent, Mike Leigh, Max Stafford-Clark, Joint Stock, Eclipse, Talawa, Tamasha, Graeae and Punchdrunk.
Know designers such as Chitty, Crowley, Koltai, Napier, Piper, Smith, Constable, Rippeth, Fry, Pool and puppetry makers Handspring and Olie.
Choose one, two or three specialisms for text-based work.
Interpret texts, communicate meaning and realise artistic intention in text-based drama.
Analyse and evaluate own work.
Study a second, different prescribed practitioner in the same detail.
Connect theory and practice across periods, styles and contexts, and how theatre makers collaborate.
Explore three key extracts from different plays, perform or design one, and show the practitioner's influence.
